summary: Fresh mobile web preview testing verified email login, dashboard seeded Velvet Cedar data, note balance chart, and responsive four-tab shell. Backend logs showed successful auth and formula/ingredient requests. Deeper automation was partly blocked by duplicate visible text labels and missing testIDs, not a confirmed product failure.
action_items: Add data-testid/testID attributes to login controls, tab triggers, add-material modal fields, calculator inputs, formula actions, and sign-out controls to enable reliable regression coverage.

Use the required EXPO_BACKEND_URL/configured native fallback naming in the API client; current api.ts only reads EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL while frontend/.env provides EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL and the requested contract names EXPO_BACKEND_URL.
Run a follow-up authenticated end-to-end test for formula create/edit/duplicate/share and ingredient save after stable testIDs are added.
critical_code_review_comments: Several interactive elements have no testID, reducing automated coverage and making duplicate text selectors ambiguous.
The web API origin fallback avoided the stale formula-atelier CORS issue in this preview, but the native URL fallback does not follow the requested EXPO_BACKEND_URL contract.
Expo logs contain a root Electron sandbox/React Native DevTools warning; Metro still bundles and serves successfully.

success_rate.frontend: 70% (login/dashboard/tabs shell partially verified; deep flows blocked by selector ambiguity)

seed_data_creation: None. Existing seeded Bergamot, Hedione, Iso E Super, Ambroxan, Cedarwood, and Velvet Cedar were observed.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Credentials were read from /app/memory/test_credentials.md. Fresh login succeeded with studio@aromaform.app. Sign-out was also exercised once and returned to login. No mocked APIs observed.
rca_of_issue: Automation ambiguity is caused by missing testIDs and repeated visible labels (for example Velvet Cedar and Raw materials appear more than once), producing strict-mode failures. This is a testability gap rather than confirmed runtime breakage.
